label: D1 fixation step in the early part of the episode (trials ~2-30), after a rewarded or common previous trial
explanation: Fires almost only at D1 (93% of activation mass; never at GO, a little at D2). It works like an episode-time clock: the D1 firing rate is about 0.2 on trials 0-29, falls through trials 30-49, and is about zero from trial 50 on. It does not fire on trials 0-1. Within that window it is boosted when the reward input is 1 (in_rew=1 holds 75% of mass) and when the previous transition was common; it is suppressed after rare transitions (prev_common=0 rate 0.013). It is weakly biased toward a1/S1 histories. Activations concentrate where the value-head output is in a narrow middle band (7.54-7.73, 80% of mass), which is consistent with the early-episode regime. Uses only observed variables. Simpler alternatives scored lower: D1 & ep_trial<30 (F1 0.57, mass recall 0.85) and D1 & in_rew==1 (F1 0.28). Precision stays around 0.55 because many early-episode D1 steps that meet the predicate do not fire, so the description is incomplete. Magnitude claims beyond these rate and mass tables were not checked.
